images.caption: PolyMesh pipeline: STEP/B-rep CAD through feature analysis and a gradient-limited sizing field into the hybrid meshers, unified FE+VEM assembly, solve, ZZ error estimate and the hp-adapt decision that feeds back into the sizing field.

The learned mesh advisor under a DOF budget (ADR-0034): each point is a real CLI run's chosen action — predicted per-case relative error vs the --advisor-max-dof cap — with over-budget empties answered by an honest refusal, never an unaffordable action.

Feature-graded vs PolyMesh's own frozen uniform tet10 baseline on the D6 L-domain: 6,384 -> 1,248 DOF and 2.762 s -> 0.227 s at the same energy deficit band. Internal self-comparison, not a comparison against any external solver.

Method-of-manufactured-solutions energy-norm convergence: frozen P1 elements at 0.997/0.997/2.000/2.000 against theory 1/1/2/2, and the hierarchical p-basis at 1.02/1.99/2.98/3.98 against theory 1/2/3/4.
Tier-1 analytical verification: every case inside tolerance, measured on structured parametric verification meshes rather than product Cartesian grid-fill meshes.

Close-up on the hole (identical camera in both panels, 40 mm window): uniform (--no-feature, h = 4.2 mm) vs feature-graded (h = 5.6 mm) sizing on the same part and mesher, h tuned to a matched element budget: 43,024 vs 45,424 cells (5.6% apart), 190,320 vs 206,436 DOF.
Tile of compare_grading.png: feature-graded sizing field, 68,812 nodes / 45,424 cells.
Tile of compare_grading.png: uniform sizing field  (--no-feature), 63,440 nodes / 43,024 cells.

Mesh-only renders of the same plate at h = 6 mm under 3 of 3 meshers — tet: 12,600 nodes / 7,200 cells · graded: 77,796 nodes / 52,016 cells · hybrid: 44,916 nodes / 9,120 cells. All are Cartesian grid-fill topologies, not Delaunay.
Tile of compare_meshers.png: graded mesher, 77,796 nodes / 52,016 cells.
Tile of compare_meshers.png: hybrid mesher, 44,916 nodes / 9,120 cells.
Tile of compare_meshers.png: tet mesher, 12,600 nodes / 7,200 cells.

Cantilever beam: von Mises stress on the graded mesh (h = 30 mm, 64,657 nodes / 44,832 elements, 193,971 DOF); root face fixed, -z resultant on tip face; displacement warped ×200; colour range 0 – 5.47 MPa (clipped at the 99th percentile of the visible surface field); peak nodal value 5.85 MPa at the clamped-face stress singularity.

Cylinder: von Mises stress on the graded mesh (h = 12 mm, 229,133 nodes / 158,584 elements, 687,399 DOF); base z < 0.015 m fixed, +z resultant on cap; displacement warped ×5000; colour range 0 – 2.93 MPa (clipped at the 99th percentile of the visible surface field); peak nodal value 3.31 MPa at the clamped-face stress singularity.

Round ice-cream cone: von Mises stress on the graded mesh (h = 10 mm, 126,889 nodes / 86,688 elements, 380,667 DOF); foot z <= 0.012 m fixed, -z resultant on scoop; displacement warped ×5000; colour range 0 – 2.96 MPa (clipped at the 99th percentile of the visible surface field); peak nodal value 4.34 MPa at the clamped-face stress singularity.

Plate with hole: von Mises stress on the graded mesh (h = 6 mm, 77,796 nodes / 52,016 elements, 233,388 DOF); min-x face fixed, +x resultant on max-x face; displacement warped ×5000; colour range 0 – 2.54 MPa (clipped at the 99th percentile of the visible surface field); peak nodal value 3.09 MPa at the clamped-face stress singularity.

Sphere: von Mises stress on the graded mesh (h = 8 mm, 173,517 nodes / 121,064 elements, 520,551 DOF); lower cap fixed, -z resultant on upper cap; displacement warped ×10000; colour range 0 – 1.66 MPa (clipped at the 99th percentile of the visible surface field); peak nodal value 3.56 MPa at the clamped-face stress singularity.

Flagship render: von Mises stress across the plate with hole on the feature-graded mesh, shot from a low oblique angle (h = 6 mm, 77,796 nodes / 52,016 elements, 233,388 DOF); min-x face fixed, +x resultant on max-x face; displacement warped ×5000; colour range 0 – 2.54 MPa (clipped at the 99th percentile of the visible surface field); peak nodal value 3.09 MPa at the clamped-face stress singularity.
